item.title: index
item.description:
Welcome to the campaign! This index serves as your central directory for all homebrew rules, character creation guidelines, and setting-specific mechanical adjustments.Please review these pages before creating your character or during gameplay: Mechanical Changes: Core rule adjustments, including strict resting on the road, flanking alternatives, custom inspiration types, tool rescaling, and concentration formulas.
Glossary: Quick reference for character creation (Heroic Dice Roll method) and combat formulas (Concentration Checks).
World Map: The high-resolution map of the continent of Londar.
Kingdom of Graodom: A diverse, trade-focused monarchy governed by a democratic council with royal oversight.
Rhiaal: A highly magical, autocratic elven empire set in deserts and jungles, with strict laws and a distinct class hierarchy.
Rotterlund: A proto-nationalist, engineering-focused mountainous dictatorship known for rare materials, whiskey, and martial discipline.
Priatar: A center-left democracy run by a coalition of beastial tribe elders, currently at war with Rhiaal.
Changed Races: Lore and mechanical details for exotic races (such as 2nd Generation Warforged) in this setting.
Banned Races: A list of races that are extinct, unavailable, or considered vermin in this world (e.g., Drow, Goblinoids, Kobolds, and certain Spelljammer/Eberron options).
Changed Classes: Key modifications to core classes (Martials, Barbarians, Clerics, Warlocks, and Wizards).
Banned Classes: Classes and sources that are not permitted (such as Blood Hunter, 5.5E Content, and general homebrew).
Changed Subclasses: Balance and usability tweaks for specific subclasses (Battle Master Fighter, Thief Rogue, and Divination Wizard).
Banned Subclasses: Restricted or banned subclasses due to balance or campaign lore (e.g., Twilight/Peace Clerics, single-level Hexblade multiclass dips, and Order of Scribes).
Changed Spells: Spell adjustments for narrative and balance purposes (e.g., Revivify soul corruption, Goodberry, Sending, Identify, and Leomund's Tiny Hut).
Banned Spells: Spells that do not exist or are strictly forbidden in this setting (e.g., Silvery Barbs). The deities of this setting, each guarding specific aspects of the world and granting distinct blessings:
Afriel: God of Nature & Guardian of the Fey-Wild.
Anubis: God of the Dead and Punishment & Guardian of the Infernal.
Aphrodite: Goddess of Love and Trust.
Ares: God of War and Battle.
Artemis: Goddess of Hunting and Sport.
Bahamut: God of the Sky & Guardian of the Dragon.
Bhaal: God of Madness, Rebirth & Murder.
Dionysus: God of Entertainment, Parties and Wine.
Hephaistos: God of the Forge and Creation.
Isis: Goddess of the Moon and Trickery & Guardian of the Moon.
Persephone: Goddess of Seasonal Change and Constant & Guardian of the Infernal.
Sol: Goddess of the Sun and Stoicism & Guardian of the Sun.
Temida: Goddess of Balance and Justice & Guardian of the Prison.
Zeus: God of the Earth, God of Lightning and God of Domination & Guardian of the Thunder.
???:

item.title: Zeus
item.description: Depictions: Zeus is an extremely well-built and aged man, with dirty blonde hair and a matching beard to go with it. Job/Role: Zeus keeps lightning from naturally striking mortals, keeps the planet spinning and keeps the planets' Electromagnetic Field intact. Follower Details: This religion is uncommon but shrines can be typically found in tribes or villages and the ruins of churches that date back to the First Man. Followers of Zeus are typically barbaric people or people that value strength among all other things such as Barbarians, Sorcerers, Pirates, Nobles etc.Core Philosophy: “Let your strength and your strength alone carry you through your life.”Common Blessing: “Unto the fury.”

item.title: Temida
item.description: Depictions: Temida is often depicted as a young woman wearing a blindfold with tied up brown hair carrying a set of golden scales with a deep rooted philosophy to make sure that there is balance; natural life and natural death. Job/Role: Temida's role is to create balance in morals, ethics and laws.Follower Details: This religion is the most common generally speaking, shrines are found in every village and churches are found in every city. Followers of Temida are generally common, ranging but not limited to Clerics, Paladins, Regular Citizens, Nobility, Druids etc.Core Philosophy: “While good and bad exist, there is always bad within good and good within bad. We must strive to seek balance in ourselves and our actions.”Common Blessing: “Blessings of Temida upon you”

item.title: Sol
item.description: Depictions: Sol is an elderly Aasimar woman looking ancient to time itself with locks of flame for hair. Job/Role: Sol keeps the sun shining and the planets in orbit.Follower Details: Churches are often found in Desert Towns or Villages as well as Shrines being found in Barbarian Camps, Jungles and Deserts. Followers of Sol are usually people who are primitive in either thinking and who hate waiting around or those that abide by stoicism and the laughter that comes from it such as Commoners, Barbarians, Desert Dwellers etcCore Philosophy: “Making the most out of every holy day we are given to ensure not a moment of the stars' efforts are wasted.”Common Blessing: “May She Shine.”

item.title: Persephone
item.description: Depictions: Persephone is a white haired slender woman with red skin and beautiful Byzantium eyes.Follower Details: Shrines to Persephone are very rare on Londar, only being able to find Ruined Churches of the First Man. Followers of Persephone either farmers and take care of the land around them, leans into anger more than they should or have Infernal Blood running through their veins such as Tieflings and beings that originate from the Infernal Domain, Rhiaalist Druids and more.Job/Role: Persephone changes the seasons and helps everything that grows thanks to the seasons to blossom. Core Philosophy: “Life always ends at the benefit of the other, denying such a necessary evil results in over-tolerance and pests forming.”Rhiaal's Blessing: "Water and Steel" Rotterlund's Blessing: "Fire and Steel"

item.title: Isis
item.description: Depictions: Isis is a decrepit Fallen Aasimar with a dishevelled white beard to match while sporting a poor posture. Job/Role: Isis keeps the moon in orbit and keeps the secrets of the night. Follower Details: This religion is somewhat hard to find but if you’re a frequent night-owl, you might’ve seen sigils in the night somewhere hidden by magic to make it only visible by moonlight such as the odd shrine and dilapidated temples in caves used for worship and teachings. Followers of Isis are typically people who are more geared to spend a lot of time in the night and people that aim for the skies in their pursuits such as Rogues, Travellers, Entertainers etc. Core Philosophy: “Enjoying the night of the moon and the privacy it holds is sacred, no moment can be sweeter under moonlit skies.”Common Blessing: “Shadows hide you.”

item.title: Hephaistos
item.description: Depictions: Hephaistos is a remarkably short person for his strength and has a bright orange beard and top-knot to match wearing baggy robes to hide his chiselled physique. Job/Role: Hephaistos creates artifacts and serves as innate curiosity. Follower Details: This religion is somewhat scarce; shrines can be find at the odd master-blacksmiths in Rotterlund, but outside of Rotterlund the religion is mostly unheard of. Followers of Hephaistos are typically people who are more inquisitive to the inner-workings of things and people that like to improve themselves for the sake of improving themselves such as Dwarves, Halflings, Artificers, Wizards, Blacksmiths, Tanners, Manual Workers etc.Core Philosophy: “Experience of the forge is the experience of man, being put through fire time and time again getting folded but getting stronger in the process.”Common Blessing: “Hammer of Gods Bless ye.”

item.title: Dionysus
item.description: Depictions: Dionysus is a charming man with luscious purple flowing hair with grape-vine hairpieces. Follower Details: There is only churches in the capitals, however shrines can be found in the odd brothel or bar. Followers of Dionysus are typically people who are followers of the creative arts or people that enjoy intoxication of decadence such as Bards, Artists, Nobles etc.Job/Role: Dionysus makes sure alcohol can be brewed and parties can thrive. Core Philosophy: “Make the most of heavenly decadence, enjoying thyself to the utmost that one can”Common Blessing: “Enjoy your drinks.”

item.title: Bhaal
item.description: Depictions : Bhaal is a ghostly white balding man with an unkempt black beard and blood red eyes. Follower Details: This religion isn’t known by most but is condemned by almost all Paladins and Clerics, so Shrines and Churches are typically constructed underground and hidden out of sight. Followers of Bhaal are typically evil and despicable people with very few exceptions.Job/Role: Bhaal makes sure death and decay exists to counterbalance. Core Philosophy: “Life and Birth is final. Death is also final.”Common Blessing: “Walk with Death.”

item.title: Bahamut
item.description: Depictions: Bahamut is a platinum dragon, gargantuan in size emitting a refined aura of vitality. Job/Role: Bahamut makes sure freedom is always an option and keeps the sky limitless. Follower Details: Churches are common in Priatar with shrines also being abundant. However, in other countries, the religion isn't heard of much, especially in Rotterlund besides one or two noble houses. Followers of Bahamut are typically people who crave freedom or are bound by traditions such as Dragonborns, Metallic Dragons, Citizens of Priatar etc.Core Philosophy: “We are owed a right to freedom not because we own it but because we were born.”Common Blessing: Only a head-nod twice.

item.title: Artemis
item.description: Depictions: Artemis is a short slender woman with pale skin, golden goat eyes and green braided hair with antler headpieces. Job/Role: Artemis makes sure fair competition and good natured rivalry exists. Follower Details: This religion is common in archers and hunters meaning you’ll find shrines in Hunting Huts or Tribal Villages, but is vehemently hated by most Druids or animal lovers meaning you’ll also find the odd desecrated shrine which has been destroyed by passing druids. Followers of this faith are typically people who desire more or enjoy the thrill of stalking prey such as Bloodhunters, Rangers, Archers, Thieves, Assassins etc.Core Philosophy: “All is fair in love, war and competition.”Common Blessing: “Blades be Sharp.”

item.title: Ares
item.description: Depictions: Ares is an exhausted looking man clad in battle-scarred armour with a minimally kept beard. Job/Role: Ares makes sure battles and wars are conducted with honour and grace. Follower Details: This religion is quite uncommon, meaning that you can only find decrepit churches and old texts. Followers to this faith are traditionally warriors with a strong ethic or are brutally honest people such as Fighters, Soldiers, Commanders etc.Core Philosophy: “To live for the adrenaline of battle and endure the hardships of battle is what it means to be stronger as a person; to be of sound body is to be of sound mind.”Common Blessing: “May your Blade strike strong.”

item.title: Afriel
item.description: Depictions: Afriel is a tall black bald man with elven features, donning green camouflage paint on his face as well as a hemp headband covered in leaf-like robes. Job/Role: Afriel makes sure nature and life can grow in the most inhospitable place. Follower Details: Churches to Afriel can be found in various villages, especially in Rhiaal as well as a multitude of Shrines in Forests and Jungles. Followers of Afriel typically either have elven blood in their veins, brutal nationalists or druidic in nature such as Druids, Animal Lovers, Clerics, Sorcerers, Elves etc.Core Philosophy: “Nature is what separates man from machine, such divine blessings should be protected.”Common Blessing: “Blessings of Afriel’s Light be upon you.”

item.title: Aphrodite
item.description: Depictions: Aphrodite is a beautiful and captivating woman, with pale skin and peach coloured long hair. Job/Role: Aphrodite makes sure love, trust and children can be born in the most inhumane of place. Follower Details: This religion has churches that often are close (if not are also in the same building) as a brothel and shrines can be found rarely at bars. Followers of Aphrodite are typically people who are looking for love, focus on being a people pleaser or are inclined to be more peaceful than others, such as Sorcerers, Bards, Diplomats, Prostitutes, Nobles etc.Core Philosophy: “Love, Passion, Ideas and Dialogue are what make man, man. Contriving one of any stunts the Love and Trust that can grow in the world.”

item.title: Anubis
item.description: Depictions: Anubis is a towering man with grey skin, ashy curly hair and wears onyx black armour with a Black Blade at his side. Job/Role: Anubis governs the River of Styx, the River of Souls. Without anyone maintaining it, the souls of the departed leave the Styx and endlessly wander. Follower Details: This religion is nearly unheard of in Londar except for the individuals that come across decrepit temples and shrines or people that dwells within the Cursed Lands; however is the most common religion in the Infernal Domain. Followers of Anubis are typically people with a strong threshold for enduring sufferance or a strong threshold for giving out sufferance such as Infernal Residents, Executioners and Various Devils.Core Philosophy: “Death is a necessity to punish unto the sins they commit, otherwise no line will be drawn.”Common Blessing: “Fire and Blood.”

item.title: Rotterlund
item.description:
Political Alignment: Proto-NationalistKing, Queen or Ruler: King MondoeDemocratic or Dictatorship: DictatorshipMain Trade: Raw Rare Materials such as Mythril and Adamantite, Commissioned Engineering and Electrical Consultation.Capital: The Castle of StormsList of Royal Family: King Mondo II, Queen Philandi I, Princess Yammi IMilitary Power (1/10): 6Armies / Enforcement: Rotterlund Royal guards in the Castle of Storms Citadel uses private security formed of in-house mages The Lord's Guards such as the Three-Housed Guards of Barad Series or Greywood Guards. General Environment: Full of Forests and Valleys, full of greenery. Only snowy in the Northern parts.When the Lich King fell, a group of rowdy outlaws took to the mountains and fighting local criminals. After a few years, their reputation had proceeded them; they had encouraged a culture of "getting good", being good not just in body but in mind too.As time went on, more and more people demanding he take up the little of King of the Lands. With his retainers support, he eventually took the throne.However, he was an awful leader; policies never passed and all that was created was a culture of strength and adapting to surroundings. During this time, a daring lone man would attempt to beat the King at his own game, battle.Beating the King, the new ruler took the throne and helped enact policies that help people and assist in rebuilding the areas mistreated by the previous King's retainers.No one knows what happened to that of the old King.Almost exclusively whiskey and rum is drank here due to the hearty natures of the drinks. Many popular whiskey brands around the world often stem from the Castle of Storms.Thanks to the exploits of the previous King and retainers, some languages went extinct. Common is still predominant, with Dwarven, Halfling and Infernal being the three big alternatives. Some also speak Draconic and Undercommon additionally. It is surprisngly common to come across those whom can't read or write here.1 | No mistreatment of another that is unjust in the eyes of Temida. 2 | Tax is yearly, with it being 20% of Annual Pay. 30% for Nobility. 3 | Slavery is outlawed; you may discuss a consensual contract lasting up to 2 years which has to be officiated by an Notary. 4 | Religion is to be only practised at designated temples, lest being arrested for being a Public Nuisance.  5 | As per the Rotterlund/Graodom Accord, practice of Necromancy outside of Healing uses are forbidden. Resurrection / Bringing Back the Dead is punishable by Death. 6 | In addition to these laws, local lords can enforce their own additional laws within their jurisdiction, so long they don't contradict laws above.
Predominant: Artemis and Temida
Uncommon: Hephaistos and Dionysus
Very Rare: Ares and Persephone Despite sometimes poor conditions, most are prideful about the country and often place heavy blame on local lords. Mandatory Service is required for at least 12 months with the Local Guards to build core strength. People from Rotterlund have a tendency to stereotype people based on looks and make assumptions quickly. Whenever a new Lord is anointed and Knights are appointed, there is always a party in the Castle of Storms. The King often does not attend these however his Council mostly do. Due to the events in Year 305 - The Great Necromancer of Gaeta Valley, Rotterlund has the lowest population of all of the developed nations. The events also Cursed the surrounding area, even seasoned Veteran's are encouraged not to explore. The Royal Guard are known to be some of the strongest soldiers that the King personally recruits. Most working class people often strive to attempt to become Royal Guards both for the prestige of strength it meant as well as the lucrative yearly salary and benefits. Arcane Advancements 1-10 / 6 - Has the Citadel for documented advancements, but is meant for more academic and archival purposes rather than progressing Arcane studies. Technological Advancements 1-10 / 9 - Due to the founding Dwarf's being naturally gifted when it comes to martial arts, they are natural iron-workers and engineers, combine that with the constant landfalls around them, they became architectural masters. This has led to an overt reliance on engineering and artificery. Divine Advancements 1-10 / 3 - Isn’t much of a monotheist country but the shackles of Private Practise can easily lead to secret radicalisation and privatisation of divine knowledge. The Working Class values familial relations, honest living and good meals. The Middle Class values Land and Wealth. The Upper Class values Academia, Adventure and Glory.

item.title: Priatar
item.description:
Political Alignment: Center-LeftKing, Queen or Ruler: NoneDemocratic or Dictatorship: Democratic Main Trade: Fish, Iron and ClayCapital: The Bastion of GonoList of Royal Family: None, ran by a Coalition of Beastial Tribe Elders (CoBTE)Military Power | 4/10Armies / Enforcement: Priatarian Allied ForcesGeneral Environment: Mostly Woodlands with a desert to the west and quarry to the north west.Coalition of Bestial Tribe Elders: Commander Xandon Belnak Collective organiser of forces and helps oversee democratic discussions headed by respective Elder's of Tribes as a neutral party. Also Commands the Military Forces Dragonborn, Elder Vachur Worroth  Provides troops for the War Leonin, Elder Boyojin Wreathgar Provides troops for the War Aarakocra, Elder Aera Palanur Provides Aerial Support for the War Lizardfolk, Elder Holnag Rishtr Provides Scouts for the War Tabaxi, Elder Inuk Slith Provides External Traders to Stimulate Economy and Scouts for the War. Tortle, Elder Bakarat Olgir Primarily acts as Spellcasting Support for the War Loxodon, Elder Calti Liopo Provides Internal Traders to Stimulate Economy and Provides Trade Vessels. The various elders once owned their own land which was divided unfairly and often squabbled over amongst the land and who's family land belonged to what race often leading to violence and discrimination. The Elves of Rhiaal would ask for main-land territory for resources promptly resulting in the elders collectively saying "no" resulting in the ensuing war. With the Kingdom of Graodom being where the extinction point was, the most high value alcohol is pre-extinction Wine, going for hundreds of gold pieces. Besides that, a common drink for most people is House Wine, Brandy and Cider from techniques developed by the various countries annexed into Graodom. Thankfully, due to their diplomatic positions internationally, they are able to import even expensive alcohols from other countries, such as Rhiaal and Rotterlund. 
Priaatar is the most diverse melting pot of languages, most citizens often speak up to six languages due to the various beastial races that work together. Besides that, Primordial and Sylvan are common alternatives for people to learn. Common is also commonly spoken due to frequent trade with the Kingdom of Graodom and Rotterlund1 | You have the freedom afforded by free-speech and allows you espouse religious, philosophical and political beliefs. This also allows others to criticise you freely.2 | Tax is yearly, with it being 10% of Annual Pay.3 | Crimes are investigated by Certified Investigators, Tortles (due to their neutrality among the council) and members of the CoBTE.4 | A small jury of local people from different walks of lives decide based on evidence present5 | Should the jury deem the crime too serious for them, they can pass this up to the CoBTE There are very diverse food palettes, ranging from the Tortles whom are mostly vegetarian to the Leonin's whom are mostly carnivorous. They are extremely distrusting of Elves. They are warmer towards Half-Elves since they are aware of their status within Rhiaal but are still slightly suspicious of them. There would be diverse schools of thought ranging from Race Separatists of Loxodons all the way to the Dragonborn's way of Collectivism. Democracy is in full-swing. Religious diversity is rather accepted!
Predominant: Bahamut and Sol
Uncommon: Anubis and Isis
Very Rare: Zeus, Arcane Advancements 3/10 - Due to historically poor aptitudes for magic, they often relied on tactics and numbers. They are under-developed in regards to Technological Advancements 6/10 - Since they have shared most of their wisdom handed down by tribes, it allowed them to at least advance their basic technology and infrastructure to a point of cohesion. Divine Advancements 4/10 - With them being at war, religious values and enlightenment have not had time to find their way to common-folk yet. Diversity has made a difference. The Working Class values Nature, Strength and Archery. The Middle Class values Magic, Trading and Luxury Items. The Upper Class values influence in the Council, Intellect and Resolve.

item.title: Kingdom of Graodom
item.description:
Political Alignment : Centre-Right, leaning Authoritarian King, Queen or Ruler : King Regem Vita, Democratic or Dictatorship : Democratic with approval from a Monarchy Main Trade : EverythingCapital : Beastead
List of Royal Family : King Ignis Regem Rex, Queen Pretio Dedit Rex (deceased, died during birth) and Prince Ignar Detis Rex (De-facto Leader of the Council of Graodom)Military Power (1/10) : 9Armies / Enforcement: The King has his Private King’s Order, as for the general public, they have the Royal Guards in the Capital and localised enforcement by Town’s / City’s GuardsGeneral Environment : Lots of Mountain Ranges, especially in the centre but apart from that primarily consists of regular plains and forests.With the Kingdom of Graodom being where the extinction point was, the most high value alcohol is pre-extinction Wine, going for hundreds of gold pieces. Besides that, a common drink for most people is House Wine, Brandy and Cider from techniques developed by the various countries annexed into Graodom. Thankfully, due to their diplomatic positions internationally, they are able to import even expensive alcohols from other countries, such as Rhiaal and Rotterlund. Often called the After the fall of the Lich King, a grand total of thirteen small nations were made within the confines of what-would-be-now Graodom. At odds against one another, aiming to compete and be the best, which resulted in most of these countries engaging in wars with neighbouring countries. This was until a bedazzling High-Elf by the name Ignis Regem Rex started to enchant people with his words, with people becoming enthralled by his sheer presence. Through diplomatic unions, Ignis Regem Rex had amassed the title “The Great King from Beyond” for his otherworldly charm.After snowballing what would soon to be an empire just off diplomatic discussions, he very quickly found himself at the helm of a great kingdom. Having aspirations of his own, he allowed for a democracy to dictate the kingdom. But these members of the Council would need King Ignis’ approval before being allowed.
With the people’s first democratic votes to recruit Council Members, they ended up voting in a fair number of people with the Prince being a clear contender for the next election. With the Council of Ten, they decide the fate of Graodom, with Prince Ignar Detis Rex being the untitled defacto Ruler of the Council due to his sway. Not much is known about the Prince since he is a very private person, however he similarly possesses his father's otherworldly charm.Ages 0-18 is home-schooling or tutors. 18+ is for advanced academics (such as Minas Academy, Apprenticeships or Private Tutoring)With the Kingdom of Graodom being where the extinction point was, the most high value alcohol is pre-extinction Wine, going for hundreds of gold pieces a drop with some bottles being worth small castles. Besides that, a common drink for most people is House Wine, Mead and Cider from techniques developed by the various countries annexed into Graodom. Thankfully, due to their diplomatic positions internationally, they are able to import even expensive alcohols from other countries, such as Rhiaal and Rotterlund. With Graodom being a very diverse place, most of the mountain dwellers simply moved to Rotterlund to feel more at home there. Resulting in the minority of races and languages to be Dwarven, Gnomish and Halfling. Most of the population follow normal social norms.1 | No Murder of another person that is unjust in the eyes of Temida. Punishable by 10 years in Solitude.
2 | Tax is yearly, with it being 12% of Annual Pay, 10% goes to the The Democratic Council of Graodom and 2% goes to the Crown. 3 | Slavery is outlawed; you may discuss a consensual contract lasting up to 2 years which has to be officiated by an Official. 4 | Robbing a Vendor results in a week per 10GP worth of value was stolen up to 10,000GP. If It exceeds this amount, they will lose one hand and receive a brand on their stump, marking them a thief.  5 |As per the Rotterlund/Graodom Accord, practice of Necromancy Magic outside of Healing Magic are forbidden. 6 | Investigations are to be conducted in three levels; first is Town/Village/City Court, second is Democratic Court and thirdly High Court. Town/Village/City Court is for small crimes such as theft under 100GP and general disorganised crime. Adventurers are free to come and assist with such cases. A closed jury of ten random people of the town alongside three guards will decide their punishment.Democratic Court Level is for bigger scale crimes such as corruption, theft under 1,000GP, Murder and organised crime. Adventurers are requested to attain Investigation Permits and Signed Documentation from the respective Captain of the Town. A Jury consisting of investigators, guards and a captain (depending on the severity) are to pass judgement.
High Court Level is for treasonous crimes such as plots to overthrow royalty, theft under 100,000GP. Adventurers are required to attain a Royal Decree of Investigative Immunity signed by the entire Democratic Council of Graodom or The King himself. Only the The Democratic Council of Graodom may decide their punishment, the King can only issue a punishment if the crime committed was Treason or Extreme Blasphemy/Worship of Bhaal.1 | Electoral Integrity and Candidacy - All prospective candidates for the Council of Ten, as well as local mayoralties, must undergo a formal vetting process by the current Council to ensure their platforms align with the stability of Graodom. Furthermore, the use of Enchantment or Charm magic to influence voters or political rivals is strictly prohibited and constitutes electoral treason. 2 | Guild and Commerce Regulation - As the trade capital of the world, all merchant guilds, artisan collectives, and private enterprises must register with the Council’s Bureau of Commerce. Monopolies are heavily restricted and can only operate if granted a special "Crown & Council Economic Charter." 3 | Public Assembly and Order - To maintain the peace established by the King, public demonstrations, protests, or unsanctioned gatherings exceeding thirty individuals require a permit issued by the local Democratic Court at least one week in advance. Unauthorized gatherings will be dispersed by the City Guards. 4 | Adventurer and Mercenary Oversight - Independent contractors, adventurers, and mercenary bands operating within Graodom must register for an official Guild License. Any dungeon wealth, bounties, or ancient artifacts recovered within Graodom’s borders must be declared to the Council for proper assessment of the 5% Royal Tax. 5 | Regional Autonomy and Zoning - Recognizing the cultural divide of the Kingdom, Western agricultural zones and Eastern metropolitan sectors are granted the right to establish local economic bylaws. However, these local laws cannot contradict Royal Laws, Council mandates, or the established religious exemptions of the Hallowed City of Eden and Dragon's Nest. 6 | Academic and Arcane Export - Given the preservation of knowledge at Minas Academy, the export of highly volatile magical artifacts, pre-extinction technologies, or restricted arcane texts across Graodom’s borders requires a written permit signed by at least three members of the Council of Ten. 7 | Infrastructure and Expansion - Any new construction, excavation, or expansion of settlements into the central mountain ranges must be approved by the Council to ensure it does not disrupt established trade routes or unearth dangerous pre-extinction ruins. The Midnight Curfew: To prevent disorganised crime, citizens and visitors must be indoors or within a licensed tavern by the ringing of the midnight bell. Anyone walking the streets after hours must carry a lit lantern and a valid night-pass. Peace-Bonding of Weapons: While citizens and adventurers may carry weapons, all bladed weapons must be peace-bonded (tied into their sheaths) while within the city walls or market districts. Unsheathing a weapon without cause is treated as a public disturbance. However, these local laws cannot contradict Royal Laws, Council mandates, or the established religious exemptions of the Hallowed City of Eden and Dragon's Nest. 6 | Academic and Arcane Export -t coin to afford housing. "Rough sleeping" in alleys or public squares is punishable by forced labor or exile from the town limits. Gate and Bridge Tolls: A local toll of 2 copper pieces per pedestrian and 1 silver piece per cart is required to enter the town gates or cross the lord's bridge, funding local guard salaries and road maintenance. Market Stall Licensing: No goods may be sold on the streets without a local vendor's permit. Selling counterfeit, spoiled, or unlicensed goods results in the confiscation of the cart and a fine payable to the local lord. The Guild Mandate: Any artisan (blacksmith, alchemist, brewer) operating within the jurisdiction must pay dues to the local chapter of their respective guild to ensure quality control and prevent undercutting local economies. The Lord's Woods (Poaching Laws): Hunting deer or boar, or logging for timber in designated "Lord's Forests" is strictly prohibited without a purchased writ. Gathering fallen branches or foraging for mushrooms/berries is permitted for the working class. Livestock Zoning: No livestock larger than a dog may be kept within the inner city walls. All cattle, sheep, and large mounts must be stabled or grazed in the designated outer agricultural ring. Water Rights: Diverting water from the main river for private agricultural or industrial use requires a permit. Dumping waste from tanneries, butcheries, or alchemy shops into the upstream water supply is heavily fined. Arcane Disturbance Ordinance: Casting evocation or illusion magic within the town square that causes panic, property damage, or disruption of trade is punishable by a heavy fine or time in the local stocks. Bounty Registration: Adventurers seeking to hunt monsters or bandits within the local lord's territory must register their intent with the local guard captain. This prevents mercenaries from claiming "bounties" on innocent locals or disrupting local guard investigations. 19th - 26th of September is a time of celebration for the King and Prince's Birthday and the Late-Queen's Deathday, most shops will have sales on so they can close shop and go party since both the Council of Graodom and Royal Family will donate gold, alcohol and food for festivities. In terms of population density, this place is easily the lowest despite having the highest population; many humble farmers live in the west of Graodom with some unmarked villages even cropping up here and there.
The Kingdom of Graodom was founded Temida's ethos as a fundamental basis. As a result, the Church of Temida coincide with the Crown and act independently of the The Democratic Council of Graodom. Due to the history of the Kingdom of Graodom, the lands and the traditions there-in can vastly differ from place to place. In the West, people are more modest and humble, living quiet lives surrounded by monuments and architecture predating the Lich King. In the East, people live more grandiose lives, chasing dreams and high-paying jobs.
Two places are given religious exemption from The Democratic Council of Graodom, being the Hallowed City of Eden and Dragon's Nest. Due to the religious nature surrounding these places, they are granted the Protection of the Crown and operate under their own rules/laws local to the land. In terms of religion, the most common religion is Temida however there is a bleed of Afriel supporters originating from Rhiaal but most besides the Hallowed City of Eden are more passive with their beliefs. Supporters of Artemis and are also common to the 
Predominant: Temida
Uncommon: Persephone, Afriel, Dionysus
Very Rare: Bhaal, Anubis and Ares Arcane Advancements 1-10 / 6 - Thanks to Minas Academy having preserved lots of spell scrolls and countless arcane studies, they were able to reverse engineer most of the knowledge lost to time. Technological Advancements 1-10 / 6 - Thanks to Minas Academy having preserved lots of architectural information and countless schematics, they were able to reverse engineer most of the knowledge lost to time. Divine Advancements 1-10 / 7 - Due to the foundations of which the Kingdom was found upon and the King's countless charities aimed towards preserving religious sites, countless annexed countries and their religious histories were stored. The Working Class values simple living and self-sufficiency. The Middle Class values the Creative Endeavours and the ability to chase dreams. The Upper Class values the Arcane Arts and studies surrounding the Divine.

item.title: Mechanical Changes
item.description: You can use strategy and roleplay to gain advantages during fights. Flanking is boring and lazy, I prefer to reward roleplay and in-game strategy. You can only Long Rest at Inns / Homes, Long Resting focusses more on mental fatigue and the ability to unwind. When you are on the road/not at an inn or home. However, you can Short Rest even in Dungeons so long as you have 1 hour spare. Long Rests for everyone (including Elves and any species that says otherwise) is 8 hours. Due to the nature of the campaign, you're characters will often not feel safe on the road and stay alert. Those "Long Rests" are where you're able to lower your guard without punishment. Heroic Inspirations more than likely will be handed out like candy, these can be used to roll any d20 (attack roll, saving throw, skill check etc) at advantage. Using it on a Disadvantage Role causes it to become a Neutral Roll (Roll-Once). Using it on an Advantage Role does nothing. These do not stack. Super Inspiration is handed down either because of DM mistakes or Player's feeling shafted by something. This turns any roll into an advantage roll. Using it on a Disadvantage Roll lets you re-roll any roll (Attack Roll, Damage Roll, Encounter Roll, etc) again at Advantage. Using it on an Advantage Roll lets you roll once more at Advantage, you must take the highest option of all four rolls though. These do stack! Dramatic Inspirations are handed once per session and do not roll over to the next session, they contain abilities ranging from the mundane ranging to the game-breaking. You are not allowed to disclose what your Dramatic is to the players until the end of the session to avoid colluding. At the start of the session, you will be asked to roll a 1d100 and a 1d20 for the corresponding Dramatic Inspiration. There are rare occasions that these will stack. Heroic Inspirations are pretty standard, Super Inspirations also exist because I am not perfect and will make mistakes. Dramatic Inspirations help provide an element of controlled chaos and can let a player have the ability to completely flip the dynamics in a moments notice. Your characters aren't brain dead, they will eat and drink when they need to. Sure, while those "Feast Moments" are nice, we don't need to play Rust. Your gear and rations don't maintain themselves, after an indiscriminate amount of time you will need to cough up coin to stock up on rations and maintenance supplies for your gear. Mainly an addition to the rule of common sense, while "Shopping Sessions" are nice, spending 2 hours discussing the logistics of travel is rather tedious and can take away from the flow. Think of it as background maintenance. Tools like Thieves' Tool are rolled using the [Associated Ability Roll]+[Modifier]+[Proficiency Bonus] if proficient. The tools are assigned as such: Strength: Carpenter's Tools, Cobbler's Tools, Mason's Tools, Smith's Tools, Woodcarver's Tools Dexterity: Calligrapher's Supplies, Potter's Tools, Leatherworker's Tools, Painter's Supplies, Weaver's Tools, Thieves' Tools Constitution: Glassblower's Tools Intelligence: Tinker's Tools, Gaming Sets, Navigator's Tools Wisdom: Alchemist's Supplies, Brewer's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Cook's Utensils, Jeweller's Tools, Herbalism Kit, Poisoner's Kit, Land Vehicles, Water Vehicles Charisma: Disguise Kit, Forgery Kit, Musical Instruments I personally think this helps set Thieves and Artificers above others in-terms of tool usage. Formula is DC = 10 + Spell Level + (Damage Received / 4) Scales better in my personal opinion No Silver or Copper. Self Explanatory. I know what you're thinking "What the fuck is Electrum and why are we using it!?", you'll learn in time in regards to Electrum. Gold is used for largely everything in the Overworld. There is homebrew Pantheon (with familiar names, no doubt). However, knowledge of some gods is higher than others. To be decided. The choices are Double Damage Dice or Double Damage. We'll more than likely discuss it Session 1 or Session 0. Each Level of Exhaustion instead provides a cumulative -2 to all attack rolls, saving throws and ability checks. Your Spell DC is lowered by the same amount as your exhaustion levels. Your Speed is reduced by 5 X [Exhaustion Level] in feet. You die when this reaches Level 6. A Long Rest alleviated one level of exhaustion. Spending a Week Downtime in a somewhere you own or an inn you rented automatically clears all levels of exhaustion (provided you are able to get consistent long-rests through the week). I just don't like remembering all of the effects of the different levels of exhaustion honestly lol Magic Items use Sane Magical Item Prices as a foundation. Price will also vary dependant on location and vendor. This keeps players checking other vendors rather than just relying on the first one they meet. While it more than likely sounds expensive, due to having no Copper or Silver, this will likely be easily attainable. Ability Scores are rolled using a Homebrew Method. Roll 24d6 until you get a result higher than 90 but lower than 120, drop the two highest and the two lowest. Then Group them into three's and add them up in their respective groups, those are your scores. [6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1] becomes [5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2] which then becomes [15, 15, 13, 12, 9, 8] You guy's aren't just your average run of the mill adventurers... You're special! You don't know why yet though...

item.description: Political Alignment: Right-Authoritarian King, Queen or Ruler: Queen Regent Zylen Imryth, Leader of the Rhiaalist Empire, The Unbreakable and Tamer of the Peacekeeper Democratic or Dictatorship : Autocratic DictatorshipMain Trade: Magic Items, Luxurious Items and ConquestCapital: QifalsList of Royal Family: Queen Regent, aside from that, there is a Council that advises and has authority second to the Queen; Farran Tiltatha, Spear of Rhiaal, Highest Ranking Mage and Supreme Commander of the Rhiaalist Empire (High Elf) Esmyl Ranath, Leader of the Reconnaissance Division (Changeling) Khandar Brill, Commander of the Infantry Division (Dragonborn) Bengi Wrothiss, Governing Leader of the R&D Division (Wood Elf) Military Power | 9/10Armies / Enforcement: The Unified Forces of the Rhiaalist EmpireGeneral Environment: Almost entirely jungles and deserts.After the fall of the Lich King, the Remnants of Humanity thought it only fair that the elves were due restitutions due to their Drow brethren being brought to extinction by the masses due to their fear manifesting as hatred in the Drow. Assigned to the small hostile island of Qifal, the Elven people had to fight monstrous beasts on the island and were still getting slowly picked off on their new homeland.After a decade or two of fighting beasts, the Elven people found themselves not only stronger and more prideful as a result, but that the Island of Qifals was found to have no good long-term source of resources. After brainstorming, the governing Elves realised that it was a fruitless endeavour to force the earth to bear rewards so they sought to begin international diplomatic discussions for a piece of mainland so that they could gain some semblance of main-land resource only to be met with disrespectful no's with one elder even uttering "over our dead bodies" which had a lasting impact on their perspectives regarding Beastial Races especially.After a long depression, a hero among the people known only as "The Ashen Pilgrim" had returned. The Elders recognised the Ashen Pilgrim and pleaded for them to save their country in exchange for keeping her history secret, thus along with a mage, she would attempt diplomatic negotiations once more in order to try to extend the branch one last time, only for them to be told "over their dead body" once more. Thus, the two alone waged war on the scattered tribes stealing land through conquest and overwhelming strength starting the ensuing war.Following this show of strength, the first generation of Elves were rampant militants, often breeding for the sake of creating future soldiers in their eyes. The now Queen of Rhiaal aptly rose to power after the Elders unanimously named her the Leader of the Rhiaalist Empire, The Unbreakable, The Shield of Rhiaal and Tamer of the Peacekeeper. The second generation, growing close to the front lines would be exposed much more to the cruelty that befell those soldiers whom did not surrender and were taken in as slaves indentured to Nobles/Elders for "restitution".Due to their time being in Jungle Environments, Vodka with Snake Venom became a staple among Elites and Elders. As their might and borders increased, so did the production of the variety of alcohols with ciders being a main-stay for younger Rhiaalists. Most will opt to speak Elven, only when speaking with an outsider will they speak Common however they will not hesitate to talk behind an outsiders back in Elven or Sylvan.1 | The Queen's will shall be followed. Should she ask for your whole harvest, you will ask for how long.2 | The Council's unanimous desire shall be followed second. Should they demand you fly, you ask where to.3 | No animal is to be harmed. Meat may be harvested from a dead animal of natural causes.4 | Robbing a Vendor in the Robber being enslaved for a month for each 10GP worth of items stolen to a maximum of 10,000GP. Past 10,000GP, it is death. If you are hungry, grow thy food rather than steal. 5 | Only Outsiders (not Elves) with a Diplomatic or Trading Certificate may come into the lands, if an Outsider is asked for their papers and don’t have them they are prone to immediate exile.6 | Investigations are exclusively to be handled by Certified Investigators or Scout Rank Lieutenants or higher, anyone found to be casting Magic at a Crime Scene will be considered an accomplice.7 | Elders or Head's of Noble Houses may own Slaves, if someone of non-noble descent is discovered to own a Slave, said slave will be sold at an auction to the nobles.8 | No Tax on sales, money you earn is yours. It’s very common for people to be Vegetarian. While military Service isn't mandatory, it is highly encouraged by peers and societal pressure since it's one of the highest paying jobs. Non-Elves are called “Outsiders”. Outsiders are treated like Third Class beings, often shunned and not engaged with. Half-Elves are treated like Second-Class Beings, often being shunned by older generations, nobles and traditional folk but are still treated like equals by younger and more common elves. Resulting in Half-Elf Orphanages in Keylin and Tenebrou Jungle. Monotheist Country; are predominantly all casual followers of Afriel. There are followers of Temida but they are uncommon and often mocked. East Rhiaal is more traditional; believing might makes right, especially after the Death of the Drow and being surrounded by mentally broken slaves. The land they take from Priatar is merely owed from their perspective and follow the Queen Zylen Imryth unwaveringly. West Rhiaal is more progressive; being at the forefront of Rhiaal's Conquest, they see how hard it is for Priatar and the hatred the captured soldiers have for them. They would settle for an apology for the mistreatment of their people and happily release all of the slaves. Predominant: Afriel Uncommon: Temida and Sol Very Rare: Isis and Aphrodite Arcane Advancements 1-10 / 9 - Due to the Elves being naturally gifted when it comes to Arcane Arts, they are natural spell-weavers and found themselves studying Magic before the Mechanical side. This has led to an overt reliance on Magic. Technological Advancements 1-10 / 7 - Due to their longevity and wisdom, they were able to mimic their technological practices before the Lich King’s Reign and abruptly increased their advancements with more resources. This reliance on old technology doesn’t keep them as progressive as Rotterlund. Divine Advancements 1-10 / 2 - Since Rhiaal is a Monotheist Country (Afriel), this has led to a tunnel vision in terms of Divine Advancement since they’re casually practising. The Working Class values Nature, Strength and Archery. The Middle Class values Magic, Trading and Luxury Items. The Upper Class values influence in the Council, Intellect and Age.

item.title: Changed Subclasses
item.description: Know your Enemy (7th level feature) allows you to alternatively spend 10 minutes observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn all of these. YES, YOU DON'T NEED TO HARASS ME 10 TIMES! Starting when you take this Archetype, when using Thieves Tools you can instead roll using Slight of Hand instead of Dexterity. This probably sounds confusing unless you read Mechanical Changes. Portent Rework; On your turn during combat, you can use it as normal, forcing either an enemy to take a lower option or forcing you to take the higher option. Outside of combat, you can only use it to influence rolls you make. (eg, Saving Throw, Skill Checks etc) When Initiative is being rolled, you can use Portent to change your own Initiative roll or an enemy that you can see. This avoids other player's agency being blatantly violated and due to the VTT nature, it's not obvious when I'm rolling everything.

item.title: Changed Classes
item.description: Those who cannot cast spells (Maximum 1st level) are granted the ability to use Strength in place of Charisma for Intimidation Checks. Additionally, you are provided a Passive Intimidation calculated Strength Roll + Modifier + Proficiency. Some will feel mildly unnerved in your presence. Keeps Martial Classes relevant, especially Barbarians. While Raging, as a bonus action, you can bang on your chest (as long as you're not wearing armor) to keep your rage going. Roll a d4 for damage, on a 1 you take no damage and keep your rage going. Haha Funny buff. Starting at level 14, whenever you make roll 9 or lower on an Acrobatics or Athletics check, treat it as a 10. Barbarians get NO love. Damn. Similar to a Paladin, you can lose your way and by proxy, your connection to your God should you squander your abilities in a way that violates your God's ethos. Should you lose your Divine Light, you will change to the War Domain. ||There will be plenty of warnings before you are cut off, just like a Paladin.|| Kinda weird how Clerics aren't beholden to the same restrictions...? This is available from Level 3 onwards instead of 10. Divine Intervention can only be attempted once per week. If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 30 days (one in-game month). Otherwise, you can use it after a week. At Level 20, this defaults back to the normal rules. This probably looks worse than it is, keep in mind that you aren't long-resting as much as you're expecting. You have the option of making requests to your patron, however the extent will be dependent on your Warlock Level, your Patron and your relationship with your Patron. At the end of the day, Warlocks are just CRAPPY Clerics that follow a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Arcane Power with actual clerics following a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Divine Power. You also have the great ability to lose your abilities dependent on the grievances of your Patron towards you personally. Similar to a Cleric losing their Divine Light, you will lose your Arcane Darkness. This will result in you pivoting to either Bard or Fighter dependent on your choice. Also kinda strange that none of the Patrons can just take their powers. This way, the experience of having magic flows can act as a catalyst for dormant latent magical potential. To Learn a Spell from a Spell-Scroll alone, It requires 500GP in materials + 24 Hours for each level. Having a Professor teach you cuts this down by half. EG) A 5th Level Scroll would cost 1,250GP + 120 hours You gain more money and this helps keep the party exploring more rather than just spending a small amount of time and gold before fucking off.

item.title: Welcome
item.description:
Welcome to the campaign! This index serves as your central directory for all homebrew rules, character creation guidelines, and setting-specific mechanical adjustments.Please review these pages before creating your character or during gameplay: Mechanical Changes: Core rule adjustments, including strict resting on the road, flanking alternatives, custom inspiration types, tool rescaling, and concentration formulas.
Changed Races: Lore and mechanical details for exotic races (such as 2nd Generation Warforged) in this setting.
Banned Races: A list of races that are extinct, unavailable, or considered vermin in this world (e.g., Drow, Goblinoids, Kobolds, and certain Spelljammer/Eberron options).
Changed Classes: Key modifications to core classes (Martials, Barbarians, Clerics, Warlocks, and Wizards).
Banned Classes: Classes and sources that are not permitted (such as Blood Hunter, 5.5E, and general homebrew).
Changed Subclasses: Balance and usability tweaks for specific subclasses (Battle Master Fighter, Thief Rogue, and Divination Wizard).
Banned Subclasses: Restricted or banned subclasses due to balance or campaign lore (e.g., Twilight/Peace Clerics, single-level Hexblade multiclass dips, and Order of Scribes).
Changed Spells: Spell adjustments for narrative and balance purposes (e.g., Revivify soul corruption, Goodberry, Sending, Identify, and Leomund's Tiny Hut).
Banned Spells: Spells that do not exist or are strictly forbidden in this setting (e.g., Silvery Barbs).

A Simulacrum cannot cast Simulacrum, a simulacrum does not have a soul or anything to draw from. No infinite bullshit for you random mage! Cures afflictions ailing the soul. Sounds weird but I'm sure it'll make sense in due time. Using it by means of a spell-slot is an exhausting process, you cannot cast Wish again for 24 hours regardless of if you have long-rested during those 24 hours. Balancing Wish is like fighting the wind lol, this is just to prevent spam for Level 20+ :KEKL:

Portent Tweak; On your turn during combat, you can use it as normal, forcing either an enemy to take a lower option or forcing you to take the higher option. item.title: Changed Classes
item.description: Those who cannot cast spells (Maximum 1st level) are granted the ability to use Strength in place of Charisma for Intimidation Checks. Additionally, you are provided a Passive Intimidation calculated Strength Roll + Modifier + Proficiency. Some will feel mildly unnerved in your presence. Keeps Martial Classes relevant, especially Barbarians. While Raging, as a bonus action, you can bang on your chest (as long as you're not wearing armor) to keep your rage going. Roll a d4 for damage, on a 1 you take no damage and keep your rage going. Haha Funny buff. Starting at level 14, whenever you make roll 9 or lower on an Acrobatics or Athletics check, treat it as a 10. Barbarians get NO love. Damn. Similar to a Paladin, you can lose your way and by proxy, your connection to your God should you squander your abilities in a way that violates your God's ethos. Should you lose your Divine Light, you will change to the War Domain. ||There will be plenty of warnings before you are cut off, just like a Paladin.|| Kinda weird how Clerics aren't beholden to the same restrictions...? This is available from Level 3 onwards instead of 10. Divine Intervention can only be attempted once per week. If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 30 days (one in-game month). Otherwise, you can use it after a week. At Level 20, this defaults back to the normal rules. This probably looks worse than it is, keep in mind that you aren't long-resting as much as you're expecting. You have the option of making requests to your patron, however the extent will be dependent on your Warlock Level, your Patron and your relationship with your Patron. At the end of the day, Warlocks are just CRAPPY Clerics that follow a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Arcane Power with actual clerics following a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Divine Power. You also have the great ability to lose your abilities dependent on the grievances of your Patron towards you personally. Similar to a Cleric losing their Divine Light, you will lose your Arcane Darkness. This will result in you pivoting to either Bard or Fighter dependent on your choice. Also kinda strange that none of the Patrons can just take their powers. This way, the experience of having magic flows can act as a catalyst for dormant latent magical potential. To Learn a Spell from a Spell-Scroll alone, It requires 500GP in materials + 24 Hours for each level. Having a Professor teach you cuts this down by half. EG) A 5th Level Scroll would cost 1,250GP + 120 hours You gain more money and this helps keep the party exploring more rather than just spending a small amount of time and gold before fucking off.
